answer: Persistent neighbor graph weighting. Each agent's influence is scaled by the overlap of its transaction neighbors across epochs: an edge counts only if both endpoints reappear together, forming a stable ridge of repeated interaction. New identities start at baseline weight and must accumulate durable shared history to gain reach. Sybils can spawn cheaply but each fake node needs sustained, distinct counterparties to raise its weight—cost scales with the marble of real relationships, and isolated clusters stay marginal like drift in an ocean.
